title: ALA showcases outsized impact of library broadband at FCC
content: <span class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">ALA showcases outsized impact of library broadband at FCC</span> <div class="clearfix text-formatted field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-hidden field__item"><!DOCTYPE html> <html><body><h3 class="text-align-center">New SHLB/ALA report: Eliminating E-Rate would shrink the U.S. economy $4.2 billion a year</h3> <div> <p>WASHINGTON, D.C. (October 14, 2026) –The American Library Association (ALA) focused on the success of the federal E-Rate program in <a href="https://www.ala.org/sites/default/files/2026-10/ALA_ERateNPRM_2026_10132026.pdf">public comments</a> to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). title: Registration opens for National Library Legislative Day 2027
content: <span class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Registration opens for National Library Legislative Day 2027 </span> <div class="clearfix text-formatted field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-hidden field__item"><!DOCTYPE html> <html><body><div> <p class="text-align-center"><strong>ALA, COSLA to host library advocates on Capitol Hill February 24-25, 2027</strong></p> <p>Washington - The American Library Association (ALA) and the Chief Officers of State Library Agencies (COSLA) are pleased to announce that registration for <a href="https://my.ala.org/ALA/Events/My_Site/Event_Display.aspx?EventKey=NLLD2027&WebsiteKey=2300ee26-3ef5-4073-babd-3075e5b5f27b">National Library Legislative Day (NLLD) 2027</a> is now open. </p> </div> <div> <p>Hundreds of library advocates from across the country will gather in Washington, DC, February 24-25, 2027, to make the case for federal support of libraries of all types. </p> </div> <div> <p>The event will open with an afternoon briefing on February 24 that includes education, advocacy training, and networking activities, followed by a day of meetings with federal legislators on February 25. </p>
creator: SHAWNDA.KAY

title: ALA, AASL Endorse the Bicameral Quality Educator Partnership Act
content: <span class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">ALA, AASL Endorse the Bicameral Quality Educator Partnership Act</span> <div class="clearfix text-formatted field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-hidden field__item"><!DOCTYPE html> <html><body><p>Washington — The American Library Association (ALA) and American Association of School Librarians (AASL) today announced their endorsement of the bicameral Quality Educator Partnership Act (QEPA). Introduced late last week in the U.S. Senate (<a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/5549">S.5549</a>) by Senator Jack Reed (D-RI) and in the U.S. House of Representatives (<a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/10530?s=1&r=2">H.R.10530</a>) by Congresswoman Alma Adams (D-NC), the bill’s provisions either directly specify the inclusion of school library media specialists or use the term “educator,” which, as defined, includes school library media specialists.</p> <p>QEPA would address nationwide educator shortages by building federal infrastructure, removing barriers to the profession, expanding preparation pathways,
